newsitem.title: USA: FAA tells L.A. to return $31 mln of airport funds.
newsitem.headline: FAA tells L.A. to return $31 mln of airport funds.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration this week ordered Los Angeles officials to return within 10 days $31 million that the FAA says the city snatched from Los Angeles International Airport.

"The funds ... should be returned to the LAX account, with interest, within 10 days," Susan Kurland, the Department of Transportation's associate administrator for airports, said in a Nov. 13 letter to John Driscoll, executive director of Los Angeles' airports department.
"The city's prompt cooperation will avoid any impact on federal assistance to ... other city programs," Kurland warned.
City officials say the U.S. owes L.A. millions of dollars for investments the city made in the airport as far back as 70 years.
But DOT says L.A. is reneging on a pact the city made with the U.S. in 1975 to accept $5.2 million as payment for remaining airport expenses.
Also under the agreement, L.A. could be reimbursed in the future only for certain services and general obligation bond repayments.
"This is a very clear case," Williams Shulz, Federal Aviation Administration's spokesman, said in a telephone interview. "We fully expect them to act appropriately."
DOT attorneys said in a November 13 memorandum, "The city has not justified its claim. Therefore, the city should be required to take corrective action."

John Ferraro, president of the L.A. city counsel, said in a Nov. 13 letter to DOT Secretary Federico Pena that the city has placed the funds in a special account. L.A. "has no intention of spending them until a further audit determines the amounts which are legally due and owing," he said.

Ferraro said the city has hired a major accounting firm to "investigate, review and audit" city records to see if L.A.'s shift of airport dollars to its general account to pay police, firefighters, and other bills is legal.
Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz, chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee's aviation subpanel, recently called L.A.'s actions a "middle-of-the-night scheme" that blatantly "circumvents" federal law.
"The city's action will not fool anyone," McCain said. If L.A. does not transfer the $31 million, McCain said he will try to slash the city's federal airport funding.
Title 8 of a new bill enacted by Congress bars municipalities from diverting federal airport dollars.
Under the bill, the Federal Aviation Reauthorization Act of 1996, cities can ask the federal government to reimburse them for contributions they have made to airports for only the past six years.
Mccain first introduced the bill in May to reverse waht he called an "alarming" trend by localities to divert airport dollars for non-airport purposes.
He charged that over $170 million has been snared between 1992 and 1995.
